name: Powwow song
lineage: Plains-Northern intertribal Native American powwow drum-circle song tradition — the pan-tribal Native American performance format that emerged in the late-19th-century post-reservation period from older tribal-specific song traditions (Plains Lakota / Dakota / Crow, Great Lakes Ojibwe, Northern Plains Cree) and codified through the 20th century into an intertribal cultural-renewal celebration network; performed on the powwow drum (a single large frame drum shared by 6-10 drummers in a circle) with unison falsetto-high vocable lyrics — drum groups: Black Lodge Singers (Blackfeet), Northern Cree Singers, Whitefish Bay Singers (Ojibwe)
